impact: VAL-CAP-006 (N-008 row 181, smoke / must-pass / regression, M1 / 1080p60 / NVENC) failed its leg 1 criterion ("declared frame count produced even while source window is minimised or behind another window for the full 60 s") during retry-2 execution on 2026-05-22T18:54:27→18:58:50Z. Leg 2 (HUD timer increments) passed. Net row verdict: BLOCKED on leg 1 → must-pass red blocking T-010c §22 smoke. Evidence: ffprobe on the v2 export file at `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/cove-screen-recorder/exports/exp-1779476330387946665-0003.mp4` (87 122 333 bytes; ISO MP4 / h264 / 3840x2160 / r_frame_rate=120/1 / avg_frame_rate≈43.08 fps / duration=27.856178s / nb_read_frames=1200 = nb_read_packets=1200). Per N-008 §6.1 line 409, declared frame count = round(duration × declared_fps) = round(27.856 × 60) = 1671 at the UI preset's declared 60 fps; 1200 actual = 71.8% of declared, deficit 28%. Earlier draft of the row's evidence file (.story/handovers/evidence/2026-05-22-t-010c-slice-3-m1-smoke-completion-retry-2/operator-evidence/VAL-CAP-006/) marked the row PASS by re-interpreting through VAL-EXP-011's "real cadence preserved" lens; Codex review 2026-05-22T16:43:28 (Issue #1) correctly rejected that re-interpretation. Test conditions during the failure run: (a) source actually captured at 3840x2160 (DP-4 had been pre-flight-set to 1920x1080@60 via kscreen-doctor at slice start but KDE-Plasma auto-restored its preferred 3840x2160@240 mode at some point before/during the capture; no `capture.formatChanged` notification observed in the helper slice), (b) DMA-BUF negotiation hard-failed on both portal sessions in the row (18:54:27.103Z + 18:57:17.648Z); helper transparently fell back to SHM, (c) the Cove window was occluded for ≥60 s of the recording window per row procedure (operator-confirmed coverage maneuver; HUD jumped from 00:05 to 01:15 across the cover-and-restore sequence). Possible root causes to triage: (i) KWin's PipeWire screencast natively throttles frame emission when the source compositor surface is occluded and the desktop is largely idle — frames may be supply-limited at the compositor boundary, in which case this is documented Wayland behavior and the criterion may need refinement for occluded-source rows; (ii) SHM fallback's per-frame copy overhead may not sustain 60 Hz at 4K; (iii) the helper's NVENC encoder may not be receiving frames at nominal rate when running against a 4K source under SHM. Re-test conditions to disambiguate: rerun VAL-CAP-006 at confirmed 1920x1080@60 source (kscreen-doctor verified at row start AND just before save), Cove visible during coverage (replace minimise with another fullscreen window layered above; allow KWin to keep compositing the captured display so frame supply isn't supply-limited), fresh DMA-BUF path (restart helper with cleared restore token to force fresh portal handshake; verify DMA-BUF succeeds before relying on its frame rate). If at 1080p60 + DMA-BUF + occluded-but-active compositor the helper still misses declared count by more than the §6.1 ±5% 99th percentile budget, this is a real capture/encoder defect; if it passes, the original failure may be a test-environment artifact specific to 4K+SHM+idle-compositor. Owner-on-fail layer per N-008 §3: capture / encoder. Distinct from ISS-008 (no v2 UI callers — this row reached the v2 path successfully). A renderer engine.onReady subscription race was also investigated mid-pass and would have warranted its own ISS, but per operator authorization on 2026-05-22 it was not filed this pass (the prompt's "at most one new ISS-XXX.json" budget is reserved for this issue as the first must-pass row red); the race investigation is preserved in evidence at .story/handovers/evidence/2026-05-22-t-010c-slice-3-m1-smoke-completion-retry-2/blocker-initial-ready-race/ and may be filed in a follow-up pass if it resurfaces. Evidence paths: .story/handovers/evidence/2026-05-22-t-010c-slice-3-m1-smoke-completion-retry-2/operator-evidence/VAL-CAP-006/{BLOCKED.md,ffprobe-frame-count.txt,helper-log-excerpt.txt,hud-during-minimised.png,source-minimised.png}. This issue is the single new ISS filed this pass, within the prompt's "at most one new ISS-XXX.json" budget. DISPOSITION (2026-05-22): DMA-BUF hard-fails on RTX 4080 Super / NVIDIA 595.71.05 / KDE Wayland in all observed runs (both portal sessions in the retry-2 evidence). Frame-count deficit is observed under SHM fallback only — no DMA-BUF baseline exists on this hardware to compare against. ISS-011 cannot be resolved on this machine without either: (a) AMD/Intel DMA-BUF validation hardware that can complete VAL-CAP-006 under a working zero-copy path, or (b) formal cannot-validate policy support (N-008 platform-predicate update) that allows the row to be classified as not-applicable on NVIDIA/KDE stacks where DMA-BUF is unavailable. The engine.onReady subscription race investigated mid-pass has now been filed as ISS-013. The export FSM hang observed during the standalone retry-2 has been filed as ISS-012. DISPOSITION (2026-05-23): Option (b) implemented — T-027 added audit-safe cannot-validate policy to N-008 (new §26): pass/fail/cannot-validate taxonomy; cannot-validate = complete evidence-backed precondition-unavailable, neither passed nor failed, never green, never satisfies §24, parks the cell pending cross-platform validation; anti-abuse rule (cannot-validate strictly narrower than fail — incomplete/ambiguous/unsupported predicate ⇒ fall back to normal pass/fail); 3-artifact platform predicate (gpuInfo starts "nvidia:"; Wayland+KDE evidence present; helper session log shows DMA-BUF negotiation failure + SHM fallback); §24 guard (for manual rows, row-level adjudication beats suite-level automated aggregation — a skip-only or skip+pass summary is not gate-green). VAL-CAP-006 is split into VAL-CAP-006a (minimised/occluded survival + HUD timer increments [this issue's leg 2, which passed] + valid playable output — Issue #3 structural proof; existing N-008 §16/§17/§22 references resolve here) and VAL-CAP-006b (declared frame-count tolerance under zero-copy DMA-BUF — this issue's leg 1, which failed under SHM). This issue's evidence (same paths, unmoved) maps to VAL-CAP-006b. On this RTX 4080 Super / NVIDIA / KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland host the §26.4 predicate is complete, so VAL-CAP-006b is adjudicated cannot-validate (SHM-only; no zero-copy baseline on the host) — not green, does not satisfy §24, parked. cannot-validate is NOT a pass and NOT a runner verdict: no runtime/capture/export/ffmpeg-argv/cadence/threshold/verdictFromCounts/runner-status-union change was made; N-008 §6.1 thresholds unchanged; validation/rows.ts untouched (VAL-CAP-006 is a manual row with no runner driver, so the split lives in N-008 policy and §24 adjudication, not code). A real pass/fail for VAL-CAP-006b must come from AMD (VAAPI) or Intel (QSV) DMA-BUF hardware where zero-copy succeeds — tracked by follow-up T-028; if the declared-frame-count deficit persists on a confirmed working zero-copy path it is a real capture/encoder defect (fail), not cannot-validate. ISS-011 remains inprogress (parked pending T-028); it is not resolved by cannot-validate.
title: VAL-CAP-006 leg 1 declared-frame-count deficit under v2 capture: helper emits 1200 frames over 27.86 s (43.08 fps avg) where N-008 §6.1 line 409 requires round(duration × declared_fps) = 1671 at declared 60 fps, a 28% deficit; reproducible under SHM fallback + occluded compositor at 4K
